'''David Oliver Siegmund''' (born November 15, 1941)<ref>p. 114, ''Reports of the president and of the treasurer'', John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation, 1974.</ref> is an American [[statistician]] who has worked extensively on [[sequential analysis]].<ref name=pnas>[http://www.pnas.org/content/101/21/7843.full Biography of David O. Siegmund], David Appell, ''Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences'' '''101''', #21 (May 25, 2004), pp. 7843–7844, {{doi|10.1073/pnas.0402953101}}.</ref>

==Biography==
Siegmund grew up in [[Webster Groves, Missouri|Webster Groves]], [[Missouri]].  He received his [[bachelor's degree|baccalaureate]] degree, in mathematics, from [[Southern Methodist University]] in 1963, and a [[doctorate]] in statistics from [[Columbia University]] in 1966.  His Ph.D. advisor was [[Herbert Robbins]].  After being an assistant and then a full professor at Columbia, he went to [[Stanford University]] in 1976, where he is currently a professor of statistics.  He has served twice as the chair of Stanford's statistics department.<ref name=pnas /><ref name=home>[http://www-stat.stanford.edu/people/faculty/siegmund/index.html David O. Siegmund], home page at Stanford University.  Accessed on line September 17, 2010.</ref>  He has also held visiting positions at [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], the [[University of Zurich]], the [[University of Oxford]], and the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name=pnas />

==Work==
Siegmund has written with [[Herbert Robbins]] and [[Yuan-Shih Chow]] on the theory of [[optimal stopping]].  Much of his work has been on [[sequential analysis]], and he has also worked on the statistics of [[gene mapping]].<ref name=pnas />

==Awards and honors==
* [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] (1974)
* [[Humboldt Prize]] (1980)
* Elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1994)
* Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (1998)<ref>{{cite book|author=Siegmund, David|chapter=Genetic linkage analysis: An irregular statistical problem|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=291–300|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011586000}}</ref>
* Elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] (2002)<ref name=pnas />
* C. R. and Bhargavi Rao Prize in Statistics (2023)<ref>[https://science.psu.edu/stat/2023-rao-prize-conference The 2023 Rao Prize Conference, the Department of Statistics, Penn State University]</ref>

==Selected publications==
* (with Y. S. Chow and H. Robbins) ''Great Expectations: The Theory of Optimal Stopping'', Boston: Houghton Mifflin, 1971.
* (with Rupert Miller) [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2529881 Maximally Selected Chi Square Statistics], ''Biometrics'', '''38''', #4 (December 1982), pp.&nbsp;1011–1016.
* ''Sequential Analysis: Tests and Confidence Intervals'', New York: Springer, 1985, {{ISBN|0-387-96134-8}}.
* (with John D. Storey and Jonathan E. Taylor) Strong control, conservative point estimation and simultaneous conservative consistency of false discovery rates: a unified approach, ''[[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society]], Series B'' '''66''', #1 (February 2004), pp.&nbsp;187–205, {{doi|10.1111/j.1467-9868.2004.00439.x}}.
